name: DropdownMenu
intent: A short list of actions or options that opens from a Button or a ButtonFilter. One component: the trigger and the menu come from props.
usage: Use DropdownMenu for row actions, a More menu, or filter options. trigger button uses the kit Button with a chevron (or an icon-only button); trigger filter uses the kit ButtonFilter with its count. Items are data: label, optional description, icon, danger, disabled, selected and checkbox, with { divider: true } between groups. For filters, use checkbox items and closeOnSelect false. The panel is a white card with a blue top line, placed under the trigger (above it when there is no room). Long lists scroll past 280px; searchable adds a search field on top. See contracts/dropdownmenu.json for the full contract. The menu is fixed and placed under its trigger, and it keeps inside the frame it is in: the app frame when the screen sits in one, else the window. It gives up width rather than hanging outside, so a phone-width frame gets a narrower menu, not one over the edge. A portaled panel takes the theme of whatever opened it, so it is dark with a dark app frame even though it is drawn at the end of the page.

label.note: Trigger text and the menu name. Icon-only keeps it as the hidden button name.

itemShape.label: string
itemShape.icon: string? Material Symbols name. Shown in a tinted tile; on danger items it sits at the end.
itemShape.selected: boolean? Light blue row (bg-neutral-min-selected) with a check. Any item with selected set becomes a radio item.
itemShape.checkbox: boolean? Shows a kit Checkbox that follows selected. For multi-select filters.
itemShape.count: number? Shown as a kit Badge at the end of the row, like Chats 7.

items.note: Use { divider: true } as an entry to split groups.

trigger.note: button is the kit Button. filter is the kit ButtonFilter. field is a form field box, used by Select.

size.note: Trigger size. The menu itself has one size. Without a size it is md. A surrounding Density changes these sizes through the density tokens (Default values shown).

icon.note: Leading icon on the Button trigger. Icon-only defaults to more_vert.

iconOnly.note: Icon-only Button trigger, like a row More menu. label stays as its name.

count.note: Filter trigger only. Applied filters shown as a Count.

align.note: Panel edge lines up with the trigger's start or end. Use end at the right edge of a table.

closeOnSelect.note: Turn off for checkbox filters so several can be picked.

open.note: Controlled open state. Leave out to let the menu manage itself.

multiple.note: Items with selected become checkbox items and the menu stays open.

id.note: Field trigger id, for a label htmlFor.

text.note: Field trigger text. Defaults to label. With trigger filter it is the chosen value, shown as Name: value.

muted.note: Field trigger text in placeholder gray.

badge.note: Field trigger Badge after the text, like +2.

toggle.note: trigger filter only: the filter's on/off state. See ButtonFilter.

onToggle.note: trigger filter only: () => void. Splits the filter button: the name turns it on or off, the chevron opens the menu.

labelledBy.note: Field trigger: id of an outside label. The trigger is named by it plus its text.

describedBy.note: Field trigger: hint and error ids.

searchable.note: Search field at the top of the panel. Filters items by label. Focus starts in it.

empty.note: Shown when the search matches nothing.

menuWidth.note: default: the menu is at least 200 wide. field: the menu is only as wide as the trigger. Select passes it through.

useWhen: Row actions behind a More button.
A button that opens a short list of actions.
doNot: Do not invent DropdownMenuTrigger, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuItem, MenuDivider, ContextMenu or Popover cousins.
Do not use for choosing a value in a form. Use Select.
Do not put page navigation here. Use links.
Do not use more than one divider in a row, or a divider first or last.
Do not use a danger item for anything but destructive actions. Put it last, after a divider.
Do not use trigger field on its own. Use Select.
a11y: The trigger has aria-haspopup=menu, aria-expanded and aria-controls.
The panel is role=menu, named by label. Items are menuitem, menuitemradio (selected) or menuitemcheckbox (checkbox) with aria-checked.
Opening moves focus to the first item. Arrow Up on the trigger opens on the last item.
Arrow keys, Home and End move between items; disabled items are skipped. Enter or Space picks.
Escape and Tab close and return focus to the trigger. A click outside closes.
Icons are decorative. The checkbox inside a checkbox item is visual only; the item carries the state.
With searchable, focus starts in the search field. Arrow Down moves into the list, Arrow Up to the last item, Enter picks the first match.
snippet:
<DropdownMenu
  label="Actions"
  items={[
    { id: "edit", label: "Edit" },
    { id: "duplicate", label: "Duplicate" },
    { divider: true },
    { id: "delete", label: "Delete", icon: "delete", danger: true },
  ]}
  onSelect={(id) => {}}
/>

examples.usage: A Button with a chevron. The destructive action goes last, after a divider.

examples.usage: Icon-only tertiary trigger for a table row. Align end so the panel stays inside the table.

examples.usage: An icon tile and a second line help when options need explaining.
